scope: Public investor theses, platform transactions, operating cases and research. Authored evidence notes, not reproduced third-party articles.
datePolicy: A null publication date means not established from reviewed content. reviewed is the research-check date, not the publication or measurement date.

records.title: Services: The New Software
findings: Julien Bek argues that AI providers can sell completed work and address service budgets rather than only software budgets.
Already-outsourced, repeatable work is presented as an entry point; professional judgment remains a distinct capability.
The article places US outsourced accounting/audit at $50–80B and tax advisory at $30–35B in an illustrative opportunity map.
records.agpRelevance: Supports an outcome-based service proposition and acquiring existing customer relationships. It does not prescribe acquisition financing or AGP pricing.
limitations: Investor perspective, not a causal study or investment commitment.
Opportunity-map categories and methodology differ from Census NAICS revenue; do not add them or substitute them for the Census extract.
Retirement and labor-shortage headlines in the essay are not used as acquisition inventory or current statistical forecasts.

metrics.label: Illustrative tax advisory market
metrics.population: tax advisory opportunity-map category; geographic scope not separately specified

records.title: Partnering with Rillet: The Financial ERP for the AI Age
findings: Sequoia describes its Series A investment in an AI-native general ledger and ERP.
The product thesis includes multi-entity accounting, automated reconciliation and faster financial close.
records.agpRelevance: A reference for reusable accounting infrastructure and integrations, and also a potential competing supplier.
limitations: Software investment, not an accounting-firm acquisition.
A zero-day close and highly automated finance function are ambitions; they do not establish AGP staffing ratios, margins or valuation.

records.title: Partnering with Pennylane
findings: The investment thesis centers on a shared financial platform for European SMEs and their accountants.
Automatic data collection and accountant-client collaboration are intended to free professionals for advisory work.
records.agpRelevance: Supports shared client data and the accountant as a continuing trusted relationship, rather than technology alone.
limitations: European software-platform example; not US acquisition economics or a disclosed AI margin study.

records.title: The Future of Services
findings: General Catalyst describes combining applied AI, ownership of service businesses and strategic acquisitions.
Its playbook emphasizes expanded customer capabilities and revenue alongside cost reduction.
It describes portfolio ambitions of 10–20% growth and 30–40% margins, with growth including organic capability expansion and acquisitions.
records.agpRelevance: Closest investor-level reference for the proposed operating roll-up. Helps distinguish buying integration capability from supplying acquisition cash alone.
limitations: Portfolio ambitions and selected examples, not a representative realized-return dataset.
Margin definition is not standardized to AGP platform EBITDA; acquisition growth is not organic growth.
Does not validate 80% EBITDA margins or AGP’s 9× exit assumption.

records.title: Owning the outcome: AI-Native Services evaluation framework
findings: The framework evaluates market structure and demand, delivery economics, and defensibility.
It asks whether a provider can retain AI cost savings instead of losing them through price competition, and whether customers have reasons to remain.
records.agpRelevance: A diligence framework for retention, pricing power, repeatable delivery and the value of local relationships.
limitations: Investor judgment rather than measured accounting-firm performance.
Agent capability alone does not establish a durable high-margin business. Publication date was not available in reviewed content.

records.title: The Rise of Vertical AI in Accounting
findings: CAS creates recurring advisory relationships, but accounting workflows require industry-specific integrations and highly accurate outputs.
The authors report many pilots and fewer fully deployed relationships, favoring a focused initial vertical to build trust.
records.agpRelevance: Supports selecting one repeatable workflow and client niche before expanding across different firms.
limitations: Investor interviews and portfolio perspective; not an industry census.
Its 30% CAS growth statement differs from the CPA.com release’s 17% median for 2023; use the original survey definition instead of mixing the figures.

records.title: Our Investment in Accrual
findings: Accrual connects document ingestion, structured financial data, draft workpapers and CPA review.
The investor reports six hours saved on simple returns and up to 85% less preparation time on complex cases among early pilots.
records.agpRelevance: An adjacent product pattern for source-backed preparation and reviewer capacity.
limitations: Investor-reported selected pilots; sample, baseline and full cost are not disclosed.
Do not blend these claims with the separate Armanino season case or interpret the maximum as an average.

records.title: Current: majority ownership with local operators
findings: Current states that it acquires majority stakes while supplying recruiting, administration and technology.
The historical page reports more than $300M revenue, 20+ partnerships, 900 team members and 17 offices.
records.agpRelevance: Supports acquiring control while retaining an accountable local operator.
limitations: Historical snapshot, not current scale.
Purchased percentages, per-firm price, seller-note share and partner distribution rights are not disclosed.

records.title: Current: local-level rollover equity
findings: Current describes retained equity at local-firm level and central support for administration, compliance and technology.
An example grew from $20M to $45M revenue in under three years through organic growth and acquisitions.
records.agpRelevance: Reference for continuing-partner incentives and individually negotiated local equity.
limitations: Revenue growth is not EBITDA growth or partner cash distributions.
The example combines acquired and organic revenue; it does not demonstrate fivefold operating profit.
No standard retained percentage, valuation formula or buyout terms are disclosed.

records.title: Current rebrand and operating disclosure
findings: The rebrand announcement reports almost 30 firms, more than 2,000 employees and over $500M annual revenue.
Partner firms retain local branding, leadership and an equity interest.
It reports a 7,000-return Tax AI pilot and 31% average preparation-time savings.
records.agpRelevance: Evidence that an accounting platform can reach substantial scale while keeping local leadership.
limitations: Company-reported; revenue scope and run-rate convention are not fully reconciled.
Its accuracy headline differs from the OpenAI technical account; neither is a final-return correctness guarantee.
Pilot savings do not establish firm-wide EBITDA uplift.

records.title: Current network snapshot
findings: The reviewed homepage displays 54 firms, 2.5K+ employees, 39 states and four countries.
records.agpRelevance: A dated scale observation, useful alongside the announcement timeline.
limitations: Do not infer acquisition cadence from different website and press-release counts; reporting perimeter and dates differ.
Client count and consolidated profitability are not supplied.

records.title: Ascend / LevitZacks
findings: Nine partners and 51 staff joined the platform in a transaction effective March 1, 2024.
LevitZacks Corporation provides non-attest services; the independently owned licensed LevitZacks CPAs, LLP provides attest work.
records.agpRelevance: California reference for separating purchased tax/advisory operations from regulated engagements.
limitations: Transaction terms, price and ownership percentages are undisclosed.
This larger-firm example does not establish small-practice economics or approve AGP’s legal documents.

records.title: Ascend / Goering & Granatino
findings: The transaction added 40 professionals and was effective October 1, 2023.
GG Advisors LLC provides non-attest services; Goering & Granatino, P.A. remains the independent attest firm, with continuing local leadership.
records.agpRelevance: Reference for leadership continuity and shared operating support.
limitations: Price, purchased ownership and rollover percentages are undisclosed.
Leadership continuity alone does not prove retained local equity.

records.title: CBIZ completes Marcum acquisition
findings: CBIZ bought the non-attest business; CBIZ CPAs separately bought the attest business.
The announcement describes approximately $2.3B cash-and-stock transaction value and $2.8B expected combined annualized revenue.
records.agpRelevance: A large-scale transaction and entity-structure reference.
limitations: Announcement value is not a verified small-firm EBITDA multiple.
Combined acquirer revenue is not acquired-target revenue; dividing these figures does not produce a purchase multiple.

records.title: CBIZ 2025 Form 10-K/A: administrative services
findings: For 2025, CBIZ records $651.2M revenue from administrative service agreements with four independent CPA firms.
Services include personnel, systems and office infrastructure.
The filing identifies VIE/primary-beneficiary treatment but excludes the CPA entities’ operations and balances as immaterial.
records.agpRelevance: Demonstrates service-contract revenue and why legal ownership, consolidation and investor cash require separate analysis.
limitations: Administrative fees are revenue, not profit or a universal royalty.
Internal charges between consolidated AGP subsidiaries must be eliminated.
A services agreement does not automatically grant professional control.

records.title: Baker Tilly / Moss Adams combination announcement
findings: The announced combination separates licensed audit operations from advisory, tax and other services.
Principals hold equity in the advisory partnership alongside Hellman & Friedman and Valeas.
records.agpRelevance: Later-stage reference for professional leadership participating alongside institutional capital.
limitations: This source is an announcement, not closing evidence.
It does not disclose purchase price, partner allocations or the precise cash/equity structure.
International network revenue must not be treated as US combined-entity revenue.

records.title: Tax AI at Current / Thrive
findings: The participating-firm pilot processed 7,000 individual and trust returns (1040/1041).
Source files become structured fields and tax-engine drafts for practitioner review. Corrections feed categorized failures, evaluation sets and tested engineering changes.
The authors report approximately one-third less preparation time and about 50% higher throughput.
records.agpRelevance: Closest technical reference for a source-backed preparation workflow and an improvement loop supervised by tax professionals.
limitations: Bounded pilot, not all-network or multi-year performance.
Time-study method, full costs and downstream tax outcomes are incomplete.
Accuracy thresholds describe draft field completion, not autonomous filing or final-return correctness.

records.title: Armanino: leading AI adoption in tax
findings: The case covers the 2026 tax season, thousands of individual returns and six offices, with source-linked preparation integrated into CCH Axcess.
It reports a 15-minute median to draft and up to 60% fewer preparation hours on complex returns.
Reported portal acceptance is 74%; 91% of accepting clients uploaded documents.
records.agpRelevance: Reference for preparation, professional review, rollout support and adoption measurement.
limitations: Vendor-authored; no independent comparison group or complete downstream quality data.
A complex-return maximum is not an all-return average, and draft time is not completed-return time.
No general AGP or TaxSlayer integration result follows.

records.title: Smoker CPA: document extraction
findings: The vendor reports extraction falling from two hours to seven minutes per engagement, including upload, review and export.
The described practice has 600+ clients and uses extraction configured for 11 document types; people verify values before preparation.
records.agpRelevance: Narrow document-processing benchmark and a candidate pilot pattern.
limitations: Vendor-reported outcome without an independent test set, full cost or downstream tax-error data.
Practice client count is not necessarily the measured cohort. Extraction time is not total preparation time.

records.title: Elev8 CFO: bookkeeping to advisory capacity
findings: The case reports 27 migrated clients and monthly close moving from 18 to five days.
Monthly bookkeeping effort is reported at roughly 108 hours before and 20 after; freed capacity supports review and advisory work.
records.agpRelevance: A small-practice reference for converting repeatable processing into capacity.
limitations: Vendor-selected case; technology, process redesign and reporting changes are combined.
No complete cost or comparable close-quality dataset; hours are not automatically payroll savings.

records.title: Countsy: invoice processing with Vic.ai
findings: The case describes about 36,000 invoices a year, 78% on Autopilot and processing under two minutes per invoice.
Accountants handle review and exceptions around integrations with finance systems.
records.agpRelevance: AP workflow reference for document coding, exception handling and measuring automation coverage.
limitations: The page also claims 84% faster processing, but its 4–5-minute to under-two-minute figures do not establish that exact percentage; baseline definitions need reconciliation.
Coding accuracy, no-touch rate and final payment correctness are different metrics. Full costs are not disclosed.

records.title: 1-800Accountant: service automation and forecast labels
findings: The reviewed version describes more than 1,000 engagements in the first 24 hours after launch.
Its 70% inquiry-resolution figure is phrased as a future outcome; 40% growth for 2025 is also projected.
records.agpRelevance: Reference for routing repeat client inquiries while preserving specialist work.
limitations: Supersedes the archive note that described 70% as achieved.
Engagement volume is not successful resolution or customer satisfaction. Forecasts must not populate realized ROI.

records.title: Human + AI in Accounting: Early Evidence from the Field
records.publisher: Jung Ho Choi and Chloe L. Xie / Stanford GSB repository
findings: The repository version separates a survey of 277 accountants from field data on 79 client companies.
Reported associations include an 8.5% reallocation of time, 12% greater ledger granularity and a 7.5-day earlier monthly close.
The design also includes a framed classification experiment on human interaction with AI suggestions.
records.agpRelevance: Stronger measurement context than testimonials, with a rationale for human review and confidence-aware exceptions.
limitations: The accessed version is a working paper; field adoption is not randomly assigned.
The 2026 journal DOI could not be fetched during this review; do not silently mix its estimates with this version.
Survey respondents, client companies and transactions are different populations; bookkeeping findings do not establish tax-preparation ROI.

records.title: Future of Professionals 2025
findings: The online survey covered 2,275 professionals globally across several professions in February–March 2025.
Respondents anticipated five hours saved weekly from AI within the following year.
records.agpRelevance: Evidence of adoption expectations and the value of an explicit implementation strategy.
limitations: Predicted hours and monetized time value are not observed cash savings.
Multi-profession global sample cannot represent US small accounting firms by itself.
Strategy/benefit correlations do not prove causal effects.

records.title: 2024 CAS Benchmark Survey: 2023 operating results
findings: The release covers 206 participating CAS practices and 2023 results.
Median growth was 17%; median net client fees per professional were $156,250; 10% primarily used hourly billing.
records.agpRelevance: Context for recurring advisory services, pricing and capacity; not an automatic staffing formula.
limitations: Self-selected CAS sample, not all US accounting firms.
Fees per professional differ from revenue per all employees and do not establish AGP’s client fee.

metrics.label: Median net client fees per professional

records.title: Accounting and tax practice sold-business benchmarks
findings: For reported 2021–2025 sales, the median revenue multiple is 1.02× with quartiles 0.92× and 1.17×.
Median SDE multiple is 2.04×, with quartiles 1.61× and 2.66×; 2025 median sale price is $500,000.
records.agpRelevance: Small-practice entry-price context, closer to launch firms than national-platform transactions.
limitations: Selected marketplace sample; asking prices and sale prices are distinct.
SDE includes owner economics and is not EBITDA after replacement-manager compensation.
Does not establish 50% seller financing, $2M-firm pricing or a 9× platform EBITDA exit.

accessLimits.instruction: Use the versioned working-paper record; do not claim the journal text was reviewed.
Use the direct Accrual case and GC investment announcement instead.
